consensus_summary: The pearl primarily symbolizes the Kingdom of Heaven (or salvation/Christ/gospel found in it) as a treasure of supreme worth for which everything else should be surrendered, based on Matt 13:45-46; secondary associations include sacred/precious truth (Matt 7:6), the church or believer purchased by Christ, New Jerusalem glory (Rev 21:21), and occasionally worldly luxury or purity.
book_summary: The pearl is the one complete light, specifically the full moon (keseh, fulness) as the night sky's one pearl and governor of appointed times; wisdom and the bride are priced above pearls (via KJV rubies/peninim); this links to the one-pearl gates of the city as the merchant's entry at the King's gate.
consensus_core_identification: Kingdom of Heaven/Christ/salvation (or sacred precious spiritual truth) as supreme-value treasure
book_core_identification: full moon as the night sky's one complete light/pearl and governor of appointed times (wisdom and bride priced above pearls)
boundary_disagreement: Book introduces lunar/calendrical identification via Hebrew keseh, peninim, and appointed-time texts plus merchant-gate linkage, none of which appear among consensus primaries or alternatives; shared Rev 21:21 gates are re-centered on the moon rather than kingdom glory.
material_contradiction: None; the lunar core is simply unattested in the consensus rather than a direct negation of its spiritual-value claims.
rationale: Consensus cores (and all listed alternatives) uniformly identify the pearl with spiritual preciousness centered on the kingdom, Christ, church, or sacred truth drawn from the Matthean parable and related NT texts. The book's core equates pearl with the full moon as one complete light/governor of times, using OT moon and valuation passages plus word studies. No consensus primary or alternative covers this lunar/astronomical referent, so the relation is novel by absence, not refinement or material contradiction of the spiritual-value center.
strongest_objection: The printed citations omit the dominant NT bases (Matt 13:45-46, 7:6) that ground every consensus reading, relying instead on an unparalleled synthesis of moon, appointed-time, and valuation texts that standard symbolism does not treat as defining the pearl.
